newsitem.title: CHINA: China says grain supply to meet demand in future.
newsitem.headline: China says grain supply to meet demand in future.

text.p: China will need 499.2 million tonnes of grain a year by the year 2000, increasing to 550 million tonnes by 2010 and 640 million tonnes by 2030 and expects to be able to meet demand, officials said on Wednesday.

A senior Ministry of Agriculture official told a symposium in Beijing that he was sure of China's capability to ensure a balance between food supply and demand, mainly relying on domestic production, the Xinhua news agency said.
China will never loosen up on the production of grain, and the government's support for agriculture will be strengthened, the official was quoted as saying.
Analysing the potential of the increase of grain production, he said output of grain per hectare would rise by a large margin.
Statistics show only 35 percent of China's gains in agricultural output have come from the upgrading of technology and science, 25 percentage points lower than in developed countries, he said.
China's utilisation rates of water irrigation and chemical fertilisers can both rise by at least 20 percent, he said.
In addition, China has 33 million hectares of waste land suitable for cultivation, 130 million hectares of barren hills and 66 million hectares of waste sand areas that can be used.
Wang Xiaofang, an official at the State Science and Technology Commission, said China's grain output had the potential to increase by 30 to 100 percent over the longer term.
Thus by the end of 2030, when China's population reaches 1.6 billion from a current 1.2 billion, China will be able to feed its people, he said.
China is forecasting a record grain harvest of 475 million tonnes for 1996, up from a record 466 million tonnes last year.
